description: We are a team dedicated to space and space exploration!
summary:
Our SPHEREx project brings the universe closer by allowing people to explore real observations collected by NASA’s SPHEREx satellite. Using recent data directly from NASA’s AWS public data archive, the project retrieves astronomical observations in FITS format and processes them into clear, visual images of space based on selected sky coordinates.

Through the website, visitors can enter coordinates and initiate a scan. The system then downloads and processes the available observations, converts them into PNG images, and displays them as a chronological video sequence. This creates an opportunity to watch how a region of the sky changes across different observations and explore the objects within it.

To make the experience even more immersive, we also incorporated Aladin, which allows visitors to explore the sky in greater detail and view astronomical data in full color and definition. Together, these features transform real satellite observations into an interactive space exploration experience, making astronomy more accessible, engaging, and exciting.
details:
Space Finder 3000 is a website that allows users to traverse the night sky and look up a magnified video via coordinates to display. Our website uses API calls to IRSA to check whether or not the inputted coordinates have valid FITs for use and AWS to look up frames of the users specified coordinate's straight from SPHEREx's missions database. We process the FITs received from the database into viewable PNGs played in series to showcase any movement in the images, afterwards these coordinates are saved for easy look up later. If no data is to be found or inputted coordinates are invalid the tool will alert the user.

Our website has an easy to use UI that makes looking up astronomical objects and sky images from the SPHEREx missions simple and quick without having to traverse multiple databases and large directories. It also makes the frames found easy to view while showing any moving objects or details the user might be interested in.

Our project backend was made with Python using's libraries like PathLib, JSON, URLLib, CSV, Requests, and Astropy to send queries to API's and receive responses. Any calculations that are done use Math, Matplotlib, and NumPy to assist. Our frontend uses CSS and HTML for style and formatting the front facing view of our website. Our custom domain was acquired through GoDaddy and our server is hosted by Render.
